paper.title: Frontal-Brainstem Pathways Mediating Placebo Effects on Social Rejection

claims.text: Placebo treatment reduced both social pain (distress from romantic rejection) and physical heat pain compared to a control condition.
claims.evidence: Placebo treatment, compared with control, reduced both social and physical pain

claims.text: Placebo treatment increased activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) during both social pain and physical pain.
claims.evidence: Placebo treatment...increased activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) in both modalities

claims.text: Placebo altered the relationship between affective ratings and both dlPFC and PAG activity during social pain.
claims.evidence: Placebo further altered the relationship between affect and both dlPFC and PAG activity during social pain

claims.text: The behavioral placebo effects on social pain were mediated by a pathway connecting dlPFC to the periaqueductal gray (PAG).
claims.evidence: effects on behavior were mediated by a pathway connecting dlPFC to the PAG

claims.text: Placebo treatments reduce emotional distress by altering affective representations in frontal-brainstem systems.
claims.evidence: These findings suggest that placebo treatments reduce emotional distress by altering affective representations in frontal-brainstem systems

claims.text: Individuals who experience a targeted romantic rejection are 20 times more likely to develop depression than the general population.
claims.evidence: Individuals who experience a targeted romantic rejection are 20 times more likely to develop depression than the general population (Slavich et al., 2010)

claims.text: Activation of prefrontal areas including dlPFC and vmPFC influences pain by activating descending pain regulatory pathways in the brainstem, especially opioidergic mechanisms in the periaqueductal gray.
claims.evidence: activation of prefrontal areas...influences pain by activating descending pain regulatory pathways in the brainstem, especially opioidergic mechanisms in the periaqueductal gray (PAG)

claims.text: The PAG is recruited by frontal regions representing placebo-induced beliefs and expectations (especially dlPFC and vmPFC) to mediate placebo responses to both social and physical pain.
claims.evidence: We therefore hypothesized that the PAG might be recruited by frontal regions that represent placebo-induced beliefs and expectations...We predicted that activation of these prefrontal and brainstem regions would mediate placebo responses
